name: New-Hire Onboarding Automator

parameters.content:
## New-Hire Onboarding Automator

### How it works

1. HR submits a new-hire intake form (name, personal email, role, start date, practice areas).
2. Provisions a Google Workspace account for the new hire.
3. Sends a welcome email with the firm's SOP pack links and login instructions to the new hire's personal email, compliance-checked and logged through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (this template inherits OPS1 per its ticket, even though the recipient is an employee, not a client -- the opt-out/disclaimer checks are effectively a no-op here, but the audit log is still useful).
4. Schedules the firm's configured onboarding training sessions on the new hire's calendar relative to their start date.
5. Flags a firm-configured set of "good first matters" and creates a Clio task on each one for the new hire's supervising attorney to walk them through it.
6. Sends HR a kickoff summary confirming what was set up.

**This never grants real matter access or makes a hiring/role decision on anyone's behalf.** Account provisioning creates a login; assigning a first matter is a task recommendation for a human to act on, not a permissions change. Nothing here touches legal work (ABA Op. 512) -- it is HR/IT provisioning only.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first.
- [ ] Configure a Google Workspace admin credential (Directory API, user-provisioning scope) -- Super Admin required.
- [ ] Configure a Google Calendar OAuth2 credential.
- [ ] Configure a Clio OAuth2 credential (reuse if already deployed).
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Training Matters' tab -- see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, FIRM_EMAIL_DOMAIN, FIRM_SOP_LINKS, TRAINING_SESSIONS, TRAINING_MATTERS_SHEET_ID, CLIO_BASE_URL.
- [ ] Activate the workflow and wire your HR intake form to the webhook URL.

### Customization

FIRM_SOP_LINKS and TRAINING_SESSIONS are the entire content surface for the welcome email and training schedule -- edit those n8n Variables, not the code.

## Intake and account provisioning

Parses the HR submission and creates a Google Workspace account for the new hire.

## Welcome email, training schedule, and first matters

Three independent actions fan out from the same provisioning step: a compliance-checked welcome email, calendar invites for the firm's training sessions, and Clio tasks flagging a few good first matters.

## HR kickoff summary

A fourth, independent branch off the same provisioning step -- confirms to HR/the office manager that onboarding automation ran and what it did, without waiting on the other three branches to finish.

nodes.name: When New Hire Form Submitted
nodes.notes: Wire your HR intake form (Fluent Forms or similar) to POST here with the new hire's name, personal email, role, start date, and practice areas.

nodes.name: Parse New Hire Submission
nodes.notes: Field names here match common Fluent Forms defaults -- adjust to your actual HR form's field names if they differ. practice_areas is a comma-separated list, e.g. 'Personal Injury,Family Law'.

nodes.name: Build New Account Credentials
nodes.notes: FIRM_EMAIL_DOMAIN (e.g. 'smithlaw.com') is used to build the new hire's firm email address as firstname.lastname@yourdomain -- adjust the local-part pattern here if your firm uses a different convention.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ primaryEmail: $json.new_account_email, name: { givenName: $json.first_name, familyName: $json.last_name }, password: $json.temp_password, changePasswordAtNextLogin: true }) }}

nodes.name: Provision Google Workspace Account
nodes.notes: Creates the new hire's Google Workspace login. Needs a Google API (OAuth2) credential with domain-wide delegation and the admin.directory.user scope, connected to a Super Admin account -- wire it manually after import (Credentials -> New -> Google API, select this node, pick the credential). neverError is on so a failure (e.g. account already exists) doesn't halt the rest of onboarding -- checked in the next node.

nodes.name: Parse Provisioning Response
nodes.notes: Reads the previous node's raw HTTP response, not $json passthrough -- checks for a Google API error object and continues either way, since a provisioning failure shouldn't block the rest of onboarding.

nodes.name: Build Welcome Email
nodes.notes: FIRM_SOP_LINKS is a comma-separated list of 'Label|URL' pairs, e.g. 'Employee Handbook|https://...,Time Tracking Guide|https://...'.

nodes.name: Check Compliance Before Welcome Email
nodes.notes: This template inherits OPS1 per its ticket, even though the recipient is a new employee rather than a client -- the opt-out/disclaimer checks are effectively inert here, but the audit log entry is still useful for HR records.

nodes.name: Send Welcome Email
nodes.notes: Reaches back to 'Build Welcome Email' by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Skip — Recipient Opted Out
nodes.notes: Extremely unlikely for a brand-new employee, but respected the same as any other opt-out check in this catalog.

nodes.name: Build Training Session List
nodes.notes: TRAINING_SESSIONS controls the whole schedule -- edit the n8n Variable, not this code, to change session names, timing, or count.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ summary: $json.session_title + ' — ' + $json.full_name, description: 'Onboarding training for ' + $json.full_name + ' (' + $json.role + ').', start: { date: $json.session_date }, end: { date: $json.session_date }, attendees: [{ email: $json.personal_email }] }) }}

nodes.name: Schedule Training Sessions
nodes.notes: Runs once per training session from the list above, creating one all-day calendar invite each, sent to the new hire's personal email until their firm account is active. Uses a Google Calendar OAuth2 credential -- events land on the connected account's primary calendar; point it at a shared training calendar if your firm has one.

nodes.name: Fetch Training-Suitable Matters
nodes.notes: Reads the firm-maintained list of matters that are appropriate to walk a new hire through -- your team adds/removes rows here directly, this workflow never picks matters on its own.

nodes.name: Select Matters For New Hire
nodes.notes: TRAINING_MATTER_COUNT controls how many matters get flagged -- defaults to 3.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { name: `Onboarding: walk ${$json.full_name} through this matter (${$json.matter_name})`, due_at: new Date(Date.now() + 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString().slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00.000Z', matter: { id: $json.matter_id }, status: 'pending', priority: 'normal' } }) }}

nodes.name: Create Clio Onboarding Task Per Matter
nodes.notes: Creates one task per selected matter, due in 3 days, landing in your firm's normal Clio task queue for whoever picks it up -- this recommends a matter for review, it never grants the new hire real access on its own. Runs once per matter from the previous step.

nodes.name: Build Onboarding Kickoff Summary
nodes.notes: Sent immediately once provisioning finishes, without waiting for the welcome email, calendar invites, or Clio tasks to complete -- those run independently in parallel.

nodes.name: Send Onboarding Kickoff Summary
nodes.notes: Internal HR notification only, not sent to the new hire -- no guardrail wrap needed, same as other internal-only summaries in this catalog.

main.node: Create Clio Onboarding Task Per Matter

description: Fires when HR submits a new-hire intake form. Provisions a Google Workspace account, then fans out three independent actions: a compliance-checked welcome email with the firm's SOP pack links, calendar invites for the firm's configured training sessions, and Clio tasks flagging a few good first matters for the new hire's supervising attorney to walk them through. A fourth branch immediately confirms to HR what was set up. Never grants real matter access or makes a hiring decision -- account provisioning creates a login, and matter assignment is a task recommendation for a human to act on. Replaces manual HR onboarding checklists.
